title: Symbiotic-Lung-04: A Study to Learn About the Study Medicine Called PF-08634404 in Combination With Chemotherapy and With Tarlatamab, Alone or With Chemotherapy, in Adult Participants With Extensive-Stage Small Cell Lung Cancer
official: A GLOBAL PHASE 2/3 INTERVENTIONAL STUDY OF PF-08634404 IN COMBINATION WITH CHEMOTHERAPY IN PARTICIPANTS WITH EXTENSIVE STAGE SMALL CELL LUNG CANCER
summary:
This study is being done to learn more about an investigational medicine called PF-08634404 when used alone or in combination with other anti-cancer medicines in adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), a fast-growing type of lung cancer that has spread beyond the lung.

PF-08634404 is designed to target two pathways involved in cancer growth and survival. The study will also evaluate combinations with chemotherapy and tarlatamab, an approved immunotherapy that helps the body's immune system recognize and attack small cell lung cancer cells.

To join the study, participants must meet the following conditions:

* 18 years of age or older.
* Have extensive-stage small cell lung cancer confirmed by laboratory testing.
* Have measurable disease on imaging scans.
* Be in generally good physical condition and have adequate organ function.
* For most study groups, have not received prior systemic treatment for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer, although participants who received a single cycle of chemotherapy for life-threatening disease-related symptoms are eligible.

The study has two parts:

Phase 2 Researchers will evaluate the safety, tolerability, and preliminary anti-cancer activity of PF-08634404.

Participants may receive:

* PF-08634404 plus chemotherapy,
* PF-08634404 plus tarlatamab, or
* PF-08634404 plus tarlatamab and chemotherapy.

The results will help determine the recommended dose and treatment regimen for future study.

Phase 3 Researchers will compare PF-08634404 plus chemotherapy with an approved treatment regimen consisting of atezolizumab plus chemotherapy.

The goal is to determine whether PF-08634404 can improve outcomes such as overall survival.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Histologically or cytologically confirmed extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).
* For Phase 2 (except the Part B doublet cohort) and Phase 3: no prior systemic therapy for ES-SCLC. Participants who received 1 cycle of chemotherapy (without immunotherapy) for management of life-threatening ES-SCLC are eligible if all other criteria are met.
* Treatment-free for at least 6 months since last chemo/radiotherapy, among those treated (with curative intent) with prior chemo/radiotherapy for limited-stage SCLC
* Have at least one measurable lesion as the targeted lesion based on RECIST V1.1.
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1.
* Adequate organ function

Exclusion Criteria:

* Active central nervous system (CNS) lesions, including brainstem, meningeal, or spinal cord metastases/compression. Participants with adequately treated and stable brain metastases, or certain untreated asymptomatic brain metastases, may be eligible.
* Leptomeningeal disease
* Clinically significant risk of hemorrhage or fistula, including radiographic evidence of major blood vessel invasion/infiltration or tumor invasion of critical organs.
* History of another malignancy within 2 years, except for certain low-risk cancers.
* Active autoimmune diseases requiring systemic treatment within the past 2 years
* Evidence of non-infectious/drug-induced interstitial lung disease (ILD) or pneumonitis, or certain severe pulmonary conditions.
* Uncontrolled significant comorbidities within 6 months before study treatment
